| [QUESTION-265](../../../record/questions.d/QUESTION-265.md) | Is "psychopathic" a category error when said of a corporation, or can the construct, its affective features included, be assigned to a corporation functionally, and if so, what in a corporation would remorse, or its absence, be? | The owner's question of 2026-10-23: how the record stands on "corporate psychopathy", "qua treating the corporation as a sociopathic entity". | [QUESTION-300](../../../record/questions.d/QUESTION-300.md) | Is any motivation aimed at another's good and at the good of no self, however far a self can extend to include others and groups? | The owner's question, from the discussion that first raised self-categorization theory (2026-10-28 and 29). If selves can be more or less inclusive, as self-categorization theory, self-expansion and identity fusion all say, is apparently selfless action just self-interest on an enlarged self? An answer needs a criterion of the self's extent that is independent of what the agent cares about, and evidence on whether other-directed motivation survives once that extent is controlled. | Open |
| [QUESTION-472](../../../record/questions.d/QUESTION-472.md) v7 | Can a party's ability to activate another's genuine moral obligations constitute control over the terms of that other's dependence, so that the moral cost of withdrawal does what a contractual or material barrier to exit does, and if so, what separates it from ordinary reliance on someone's conscientiousness? | A's, from A30 §4 of the exchange "Assess Depp Heard Abuse" (2026-11-15), at the owner's U15 (points of contact with this record). | [QUESTION-473](../../../record/questions.d/QUESTION-473.md) v2 | When an organization has substantially contributed to the conditions that produced an agent's wrongdoing, what remains of its moral standing to blame that agent, as distinct from its authority to investigate, correct or sanction the wrongdoing? | Raised by the third review of 2026-11-16 (ChatGPT's, forwarded by the owner), from the exchange's discussion of institutions that make impossible demands, rely on their members' commitments to cover their own deficiencies, and then discipline the members who fail (A15, A17).
